author: Brian Wilson
releaseNotes: 1.29.0 — The switch attribute now stays on while a job is still outstanding, not just while the vacuum is physically moving. A job that runs the battery down leaves the vacuum docked and charging with every intention of resuming, but the switch used to flip off the moment cleaning stopped — which breaks the common on = clean next rooms / off = dock wiring, because the switch is already off when someone gets home and their "turn it off" automation has nothing to turn off, while the pending job resumes later anyway. Turning the switch off (or calling dock()/pause()) now also genuinely cancels a job that's paused for charging: the run is closed out, its rooms stay due rather than being credited, and if the vacuum starts up again on its own afterwards it's sent straight back to the dock — regardless of the "Don't let it auto-resume" setting, since an explicit stop already says what you want. 1.28.0 — New per-vacuum option, "Don't let it auto-resume" (under Low Battery Protection). When a job runs the battery down, the vacuum docks itself, charges, and then restarts that job on its own at whatever time charging happens to finish — confirmed live: an "everyone left" trigger started a rotation run at 5:57pm, the sweep advanced to the next room at 6:44pm on a 15% battery, that room ran flat at 6% by 6:51pm, and the vacuum restarted it itself at 8:35pm with everyone home again. The job is app-dispatched but the restart is the vacuum's own call, so a "dock when someone gets home" automation has nothing to catch — it fires on arrival, long before the firmware picks the job back up. With this on, a self-restarted job is sent straight back to the dock and the room stays pending for the next rotation, keeping its learned clean time. Off by default, preserving the existing finish-the-job behavior. 1.27.0 — Interrupting a room clean (dock()/pause()/off(), e.g. an automation firing when someone comes home) now sends its own notification saying what stopped it and how far in -- previously it reported as "finished cleaning," which was wrong twice over: a room cut short at minute 3 of 35 was fully credited as cleaned (dropping it from rotation for a whole cycle) and had its learned clean time overwritten with the truncated value, skewing future time-budget runs. A commanded stop is no longer treated as a finish. Multi-room batches still credit whichever rooms got their full time before the interruption. 1.26.0 — Better handling of cleans started outside Hubitat (from the Wyze app, the vacuum's own schedule, or its button), which this app detects and reports on like any other run. Two fixes from a live 2-zone Wyze-app clean: (1) such a run used to be announced as "started cleaning: whole house", which was untrue -- Wyze doesn't report which rooms/zones an externally-started run picked, so it now says so plainly, and "whole house" is claimed only when this app's own start() command kicked the run off. (2) When a job pauses at critically low battery and auto-resumes hours later (mode 11), the resume used to fire a second "started cleaning" notification as if it were a brand-new run -- it now reports it as resuming the same job, matching the finish-notification suppression added in 1.24.0.
